title: Night Talks in the Shadow-Play Hall
premise: Decades of village-temple shadow-puppet inheritance. A-Tang and A-Che are easily confused by looks; the Guan Gong shadow puppet goes intact→cracked→repaired; after the cart prop chests burn they must be avoided; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_master: Shadow-play master Gu Heng around fifty, short gray beard, worn indigo short jacket with frayed cuffs, thick-knuckled hands, steady eyes.
states.cane_weary: The same master's twilight look: hair and beard white, right leg slightly lame, leaning on a boxwood cane, indigo short jacket faded to gray-blue.
states.deceased: The master has closed his eyes in death, lying still beside the prop chests, face peaceful, no breath left.

states.young_apprentice: Young A-Tang: a lean shadow-play apprentice of fourteen or fifteen, ochre-red cloth strip at the nape, patched blue tunic, bright stubborn eyes.
states.adult_successor: Adult A-Tang: a young master in his twenties with broad shoulders and steady hands, still wearing the ochre-red cloth strip, blue tunic swapped for a fitted short jacket, calm eyes.

states.intact: A half-person-tall Guan Gong leather shadow puppet, red face, green robe, vivid gold armor, holding a Green Dragon Crescent Blade, joints laced with silk thread.
states.cracked: The same Guan Gong puppet: a crack bursts across the chest, green-robe hide curled up, blade joint loose, shadow incomplete.
states.repaired: The Guan Gong puppet's crack is stitched with a leather patch, green robe recolored, joints re-threaded, blade shadow whole again.

states.intact: A thread-bound old playbook, earth-yellow cover lettered 'Flooding the Seven Armies', fuzzy page edges, neat ink.
states.smoke_stained: The same playbook blackened by tung-oil lamp smoke on the cover, characters yellowed and blurred, corners scorched and wrinkled.

states.intact: A vermilion-painted two-wheeled cart stacked with three black-lacquer prop chests, lids studded with copper corners.
states.burned: The vermilion cart collapsed in fire, shafts charred black, chests broken apart, only twisted iron-hoop wreckage left.

states.young_rival: A-Che, whose face closely resembles young A-Tang's, ochre-green cloth strip at the nape, swaggering look, a brass shadow nail by the ear.
states.adult_rival: Adult A-Che still wears the ochre-green cloth strip and brass shadow nail by the ear; broader shoulders, deeper expression.

segments.action: At dusk Gu Heng lifts the shadow-play hall back curtain and checks the rod rack behind the white cloth screen.
A row of five tung-oil lamps hangs under the shadow-play hall beam; Gu Heng tops up oil and straightens each wick.
Two call-to-stage bells hang under the shadow-play hall eaves; Gu Heng reaches up and lets them tinkle softly.
Gu Heng hangs the Guan Gong shadow puppet on a rod and tests the blade-arm joint tightness.
Through a gap in the white cloth screen Gu Heng watches the village road darken outside.
The Guan Gong shadow puppet's red face and green robe stand vivid in the lamplight; the blade tip trembles lightly.
Gu Heng sits against a prop chest and listens to frogs outside the hall.
Gu Heng draws the chest-bottom playbook from the bottom of a black-lacquer prop chest and spreads it on his knees.
With charcoal Gu Heng marks tonight's gong cues for 'Flooding the Seven Armies' in the playbook blanks.
Gu Heng closes the playbook and tucks it back into the chest lining.
A tung-oil lamp behind the screen flickers; the Guan Gong shadow puppet's blade shadow sweeps Gu Heng's cheek.
At the morning village drying ground, Gu Heng greets young A-Tang pushing the vermilion cart prop chests.
A-Tang stops the cart prop chests at the drying-ground edge and wedges the wheels with wood.
Gu Heng points to the three leather shadow nails on the post and teaches A-Tang to read color dots and play routes.
A-Tang squats by the drying-ground earth ridge and curiously touches dew on the chili strings.
Gu Heng pats A-Tang's shoulder and explains tonight's entrance-exit cues for the shadow-play hall.
A-Tang looks back at the vermilion cart prop chests, eyes full of longing.
In the temple-fair lane, A-Che with the ochre-green cloth strip turns from behind a sugar-figure stall.

Gu Heng opens the chest-bottom playbook; the cover is blackened by tung-oil lamp smoke, corners scorched and wrinkled.

segments.action: The Guan Gong shadow puppet's blade shadow sways slowly on the cloth screen.
At spring-festival season Gu Heng rehearses day after day in the shadow-play hall.
On a high-summer afternoon Gu Heng wipes the sun-hot rod rack.
On the eve of the autumn temple fair Gu Heng alone cues blade points behind the screen.
Another New Year's Eve, Gu Heng keeps the tung-oil lamps till dawn.
At dawn Gu Heng patrols the village drying ground; the vermilion cart prop chests sit under the poplars.
Gu Heng crouches to check the shaft tenons of the cart prop chests.
Gu Heng walks to the post; those earlier three leather shadow nails still hang on the hemp rope.
A strange green-hide cart rolls across the drying ground—denser spokes, not the vermilion cart prop chests.
Gu Heng stands at the drying-ground edge noting temple-fair footprints ebbing away like a tide.
Gu Heng folds the dried screen cloth and weights it on a drying-ground stone pier.
Fire breaks at midnight; sparks spray from the shadow-play hall beam; the Guan Gong shadow puppet shakes hard.
Flames lick the white cloth screen; pale smoke-light fills the hall.
With a crack, a fissure bursts across the Guan Gong shadow puppet's chest; the blade-arm joint comes loose.

segments.action: A blue-gray replica cart rolls onto the drying ground—lower bed, nothing like the long-burned cart prop chests.
County troupe steward jumps down from the cart and talks beside Gu Heng; the two builds are close.
The steward points at the replica cart and explains the county's temporary grain-hauling loan.
The replica cart rumble-rolls away; Gu Heng alone watches it leave the drying ground.
Into the temple-fair lane comes a sugar-figure girl with a light-brown cloth strip; at a glance she somewhat resembles young A-Tang.
The girl tries handing over sugar figures, but Gu Heng shakes his head—she is not A-Tang after all.
Years later at dusk, white-haired Gu Heng leans on a boxwood cane under the blue-brick old opera stage.
